label: win; depth-2 better still; nets-robust
result: Depth-2 (allowing two slides before planning) strictly improved on single-slide: 188 of 200 unseen (11 improved / 0 worsened vs depth-1, fluke ~1 in 1000) and extra-moves-vs-perfect down to 0.944 on the standard exam (68.4% optimal) -- vs the same-budget standard search: 39/1 and 40/0 move wins. The win also replicated with entirely different networks (v14's): 36/0 move wins on unseen. Only 5 of 46 unseen slide-wins used both slides -- most of depth-2's edge comes from screening more one-slide options; noted honestly since the depth-2 config also widens the candidate pool. Caveat: the forward baseline is the original network; a re-tuned forward planner would likely narrow the gap measurement slightly (main FINDINGS 24).
conclusion: Adopted as the flagship search: two-slide roots with the strict-value nets. The ceiling break deepens (0.944 vs the pure-subgoal floor of 1.17) and survives a different-nets replicate. Frontier flagship leg running; wave-5 candidate: slide-aware TRAINING done properly (search-ranked slides, not uniform -- see v15).
note: Search-only change (no training); stochasticity is the search rng only. Gates: unseen moves 31/1 p=1.5e-8; graded moves 30/0 p=1.9e-9.
